summary.headline: Denta Water guided to 20% FY27 revenue growth, but the transcript is too garbled to confirm figures; H1 billing implies ~Rs 86 crore per quarter in H2.
summary.overview: The Q2 and H1 FY27 call for Denta Water and Infra Solutions was held with Chairman C. Mritunjaya Swamy, Executive Director Hema HM and CFO Sujit Tr. The transcript is largely garbled by transcription errors, so reported financial figures (revenue, margins, receivables, order book) cannot be reliably verified from this document. Management discussed receivables from government and PSU clients, a 20% FY27 revenue growth target, and a pending Rs 850 crore Karnataka water supply tender. Operations are concentrated in Karnataka, with wastewater and sewage treatment and irrigation (including KC Valley lift-irrigation work) as the main business lines.

financial_highlights.change: Management reportedly maintained 20% growth target; questioner noted H1 billing implies roughly Rs 86 crore per quarter needed in H2 (Rs 172+ crore total for H2)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 7,824 million (as transcribed; possibly Rs 782.4 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Unclear; a figure of 4,046 million was cited for water management projects

financial_highlights.value: Receivable days guided to around 120 days (as transcribed, unclear)
financial_highlights.change: Questioner said management guided normalisation of working capital

segments.name: Water supply (Karnataka, Jal Jeevan / AMRUT type schemes)
segments.commentary: Currently supplying drinking water under Jal Jeevan Mission projects and one AMRUT project to urban population; majority of projects reportedly nearing completion. Single project capacity up to Rs 300 crore executable standalone.

segments.name: Wastewater / sewage treatment
segments.commentary: Establishing sewage treatment sites at 10 locations across 5 Karnataka districts, using decentralised, bio-based technology (NABR-type biological plants) under a technology partnership.

segments.name: Irrigation (KC Valley lift irrigation)
segments.commentary: Cited as a strong business line; three KC Valley projects, one expected to complete by end of calendar 2026, and a further project around 25-30% complete.

guidance_outlook: Management reportedly maintained 20% revenue growth guidance for FY27, subject to H2 billing of roughly Rs 86 crore per quarter (questioner's calculation, not confirmed by management)
Working capital normalisation to around 120 days targeted (as stated by questioner; unconfirmed)
Pending Rs 850 crore Karnataka water supply and reuse tender: status unclear, management said it was being evaluated and would be bid only if profitable
Some tenders in Odisha and Madhya Pradesh were postponed; company will bid only where profitable
capex_capacity: Single-project execution capacity up to Rs 300 crore on a standalone basis (management)
Design phase for DBOT projects 3-4 months (up to 6), raw material procurement another 3-4 months
Sewage treatment sites planned at 10 locations in 5 Karnataka districts
demand_pricing: Order pipeline reportedly up around 15-20% versus prior period (garbled transcript; unconfirmed)
Management said 75-80% of projects from earlier Jal Jeevan Mission phases are nearing completion
Management denied forced payment or billing delays on projects; said issues are resolved locally
Expansion beyond Karnataka under evaluation but not yet concrete; Maharashtra and other states mentioned as targets

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Jal Jeevan Mission phases on receivables and working capital, and effect on order book conversion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around 75-80% of projects from the earlier phases are nearing completion and that no forced payment terms were applied; answer was partly unclear.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 margins recur at the levels seen in the period?
qa_highlights.answer: No clear answer recorded in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% FY27 growth guidance still intact given H1 billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reportedly reiterated the target, but the transcript is unclear.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Rs 850 crore Karnataka water supply and reuse tender, and Odisha / Madhya Pradesh bids.
qa_highlights.answer: Tenders were postponed; the company is analysing bids and will bid only where profitable, and will communicate once bids are made.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for tight working capital and inventory build.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited varying product mix across projects and infrastructure implementation timing, which led to higher inventory costs.

qa_highlights.question: Execution capacity and risks, including land, approvals and payments.
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone execution capacity up to Rs 300 crore per project; challenges such as land acquisition and approvals are resolved locally, and management said no project was delayed by these.

risks_watch: Elongated receivables and working capital cycle, particularly on government and PSU receivables
Pending tender outcomes (Rs 850 crore Karnataka tender; Odisha and Madhya Pradesh) and postponements
Q3 and Q4 revenue needed to reach the 20% growth target; H2 billing requirement
Transcript quality is poor; financial figures should be verified against the official results filing before use
summary.management_tone: Management was broadly confident about the order pipeline and execution, but answers were brief and often evasive on margins, receivables and tender timelines. Tender-related answers were deliberately noncommittal, saying bids would be placed only if profitable.
key_quotes: Our core focus is only those three projects.
A single project value up to 300 crores we are able to execute on our standalone basis.

adds.what: Sewage treatment sites at 10 locations across 5 Karnataka districts (decentralised, bio-based NABR-type plants)
Single-project execution capacity up to Rs 300 crore standalone (execution capability, not a physical plant)

growth.why: Management reportedly held a 20% FY27 revenue growth guide, but the transcript is too garbled to verify figures; backing is vague with an unconfirmed order book (Rs 782 crore as transcribed), a pending Rs 850 crore tender and sewage sites with no timeline.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sewage treatment sites planned at 10 locations across 5 Karnataka districts and single-project execution capacity up to Rs 300 crore, but no dated commissioning timeline was given and the transcript is garbled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reportedly held 20% FY27 revenue growth guidance, which needs roughly Rs 172+ crore in H2 against H1 billing, but the figures are unverified and order pipeline is reportedly up 15-20% (garbled).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; no utilisation figure was reported.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reportedly held the 20% FY27 target with H2 billing needed to hit it, and the Rs 850 crore tender is unresolved, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables are elongated on government and PSU clients, working capital is tight, and Odisha and Madhya Pradesh tenders were postponed, all of which put the 20% FY27 target at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or molecule launches were discussed; the sewage treatment plants use a technology partnership rather than a launch.

rows.label: Rs 850 crore Karnataka water supply and reuse tender
rows.why: Tender was being evaluated and would be bid only if profitable, with Odisha and Madhya Pradesh tenders postponed, so the win is conditional and not yet bid.

rows.label: Receivable days normalisation to ~120 days
rows.why: Questioner said management guided normalisation to around 120 days, but the figure is unconfirmed from the garbled transcript and management was evasive on receivables.

rows.label: Expansion beyond Karnataka (Maharashtra and others)
rows.why: Under evaluation but not concrete, with Maharashtra and other states mentioned as targets and no dated plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order pipeline and execution, with Jal Jeevan projects 75-80% nearing completion, but was evasive on margins, receivables and tender timelines; analysts pushed on whether the 20% FY27 target is still intact given H1 billing.
